text:
anya: Heads-up — I'm seeing a NaN spike after enabling the fp8 kernel on the long-prefix suite (seq_len 4096) in the nightly perf runs. Attach: https://gist.github.com/anya/longprefix-fp8-logs

kai: ugh. how big is the spike?

anya: perf-bot reported 412 NaNs in 6k requests. Throughput slightly up (~7%) but error rate unacceptable.

perf-bot: nightly-run-198123: model=redwood-xl fp8 enabled kernel=attn_fp8_v2 nan_count=412 throughput_tokens/s=12400 (baseline 11600)

sam: do we get stack traces? is it attention, kv-cache, or matmul?

anya: trace shows NaN originates in `attn_fp8_v2` when sequence lengths cross the 1024->4096 boundary during KV streaming. Logs:```
RuntimeError: NaN encountered in attention kernel at step=1024
  at attn_fp8_v2.cu:341
  at runtime/inference.cc:214
```

maria: hmm could be scale underflow in fp8 ops + long KV accumulation. Any difference if we force kv-rescale per-window?

devon: I ran a quick repro locally with `--seq 4096 --kv-rescale=off` and saw NaNs; with `--kv-rescale=per_window` it dropped to 4 NaNs. So rescale looks promising.

kai: interesting. that suggests accumulation of tiny values becomes subnormal and then operations blow up. SmoothQuant might help too (rescale activations before quant).

sam: calibration numbers? Maybe the fp8 calibration omitted long-prefix contexts in its dataset. If quant stats never saw long tails, exponents will be wrong.

anya: agreed. The fp8 calib we shipped used sequences up to 1024 only. I can kick off a calibration sweep with longer sequences. Command I'm running:```
./bin/calib_sweep --model redwood-xl --quant fp8 --seq_max 4096 --batches 50 --out calib_longprefix.json
```

perf-bot: calib-sweep queued (id=calib-198123). ETA ~45m.

maria: in the meantime we should add a kernel-selector policy to fallback to int8 for requests with prefix_len > 2048 until we prove fp8 safe at that scale. Canary only.

devon: +1. I can implement a selector rule:```
if prefix_len > 2048 and model.supports_fp8: prefer=int8_fallback
```

kai: also add numeric safeguards in the kernel: clamp intermediate exps to [-125, 125], check for inf/NaN on debug builds and return a well-defined fallback path instead of propagating.

sam: let's be careful with clamps — they can bias outputs. But for safety a debug clamp and telemetry is fine.

anya: I've opened a draft PR with telemetry and a soft-fallback for NaNs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 (WIP) — it instruments per-request nan_count and triggers fallback to int8 variant when nan_count > 0.

perf-bot: quick baseline: int8_fallback throughput_tokens/s=10900, nan_count=0 on same nightlies.

maria: action items: anya -> finish longprefix calib and upload stats; devon -> kernel-selector patch; kai -> add clamps + debug NaN checks in attn_fp8_v2; sam -> coordinate canary and update perf dashboard to show nan_count per model/route.

devon: I'll push a selector PR today and include a small cfg flag `fp8_longprefix_threshold=2048` so ops can tune.

anya: calib sweep finished (calib-198123). Preliminary result: activation scale factor increases ~3x for layers 8-12 under long contexts. Attaching snippet:```
layer 8 scale: 0.031 -> 0.096
layer12 scale: 0.020 -> 0.062
```

kai: that explains exponent overflow — existing per-tensor exponents were too small. SmoothQuant rescale per-channel may stabilize this. Can we try re-running the kernel with activation rescale applied?

anya: reprobed locally: enabling `smoothquant=on` reduces NaNs to 0 in my local run and the output deltas are tiny (perplexity change <0.2%).

sam: great. Two-step plan: 1) immediate canary with fp8 disabled for prefix>2048 + int8 fallback; 2) longer-term: include long-prefix data in fp8 calibration and enable smoothquant-per-layer by default for fp8 kernels.

maria: do we have a feature flag for smoothquant? ops needs to be able to turn off in emergency.

devon: added flag `enable_smoothquant_fp8` to runtime config in my branch. Default true for canary.

deploy-bot: Rolling canary: runtime:v2026-patch-4821 -> canary cluster (10% traffic). Patch includes selector fallback + telemetry.

anya: monitoring dashboards updated: nan_count per-model, per-route, per-kernel. I'll watch for regressions and post updates here.

sam: thanks everyone. Let's reconvene after 24h of canary telemetry. If all clear we merge the recalibrated fp8 weights and promote smoothquant default. :thumbsup:
